Getting Started

Set up your workspace, log in, and navigate the main layout.

1. Create a workspace

On the login screen, click “New to DomendraPOS? Create a workspace”. Fill in the workspace name, your admin email, currency (e.g. KSh for Kenya Shilling), and timezone. After you submit, you receive a confirmation email and your tenant (workspace) is provisioned.

2. Log in

Fig 1. The login screen
Open the login page
Navigate to https://app.domendrapos.com/login (or your tenant URL).
Enter your email
Use the email registered by your workspace admin.
Enter your password
Click the eye icon to reveal what you typed.
Use a strong password with at least 8 characters, mixing letters, numbers, and symbols.
Remember me (optional)
Tick this box to stay signed in for 30 days on this device.
Click Sign in
You are redirected to /dashboard (or /superadmin if you are a platform super-admin).
Need help?
Click the Documentation button on the login screen to open this guide.
For security, your account is locked for 5 minutes after 5 failed attempts. If you forgot your password, contact your tenant admin or use “Forgot password?” link (if enabled by your workspace).

3. Navigate the dashboard

Fig 2. The dashboard

The main layout has three regions:

Left sidebar
Collapsible rail with grouped navigation — Main, Administration, Platform.
Top app bar
Rail toggle, live clock, today's revenue, branch selector, theme toggle, user menu.
Content area
The active page (Dashboard, POS, Inventory, Reports, etc.).

4. Select a branch

Use the branch selector in the top app bar (top right). The default is “All Branches”. When you select a specific branch, all subsequent transactions, stock views, and reports are scoped to that branch.

Cashiers must select a branch before starting a POS session — sales are recorded against the active branch.

Point of Sale (POS)

Make sales fast — scan, tap, accept payments, and issue receipts.

Fig 3. The POS terminal
Select a branch
In the top app bar, choose the branch for this session.
Search or scan
Type product name/SKU or scan a barcode. The match list filters as you type.
Tap to add
Tap a product tile to add one unit. Tap again for more.
Set quantity / discount
In the cart panel, change quantities and apply line or cart-level discounts.
Choose a customer (optional)
Attach a walk-in or registered customer for loyalty and credit sales.
Take payment
Tap Cash, M-Pesa, or Card. For cash, enter the amount tendered. For M-Pesa, enter the phone number. A sale receipt prints automatically.
Open or close shift
At end of day, close your shift and print a reconciliation summary.

Payment methods

Cash

Record a cash payment. Enter the amount tendered to compute change.

M-Pesa

Mobile money. Enter customer phone number and STK push reference.

Card

Credit / debit card. Record the gateway reference for reconciliation.

POS features

Park / hold a sale
Park a cart to serve another customer, then resume it.
Customer credit
Issue credit sales to registered customers with outstanding balances.
Shift management
Open / close shifts and print shift summaries (cashier reconciliation).
Receipts
Print or email receipts; thermal printer friendly.

Inventory

Track stock-on-hand across branches, adjust quantities, transfer stock, and get low-stock alerts.

Fig 4. The inventory stock-on-hand page

Core concepts

Stock on hand
The quantity of each SKU currently in a branch.
Reorder point
The minimum stock level that triggers a low-stock alert.
Stock value
On-hand × cost price, shown per branch and in total.
ABC class
A = top 20% by value, B = next 30%, C = remaining 50%.
Adjustments
Manual increases or decreases with a documented reason.
Transfers
Inter-branch moves tracked with source and destination.

Stock movements

Adjustment
Increase or decrease stock for a SKU. Choose a reason: damage, theft, recount, sample, return.
Transfer
Move stock from one branch to another. Source loses; destination gains.
Receive
Receive goods from a supplier PO. Updates stock and accounting simultaneously.
Return
Return goods to a supplier. Creates a debit note and a payable reversal.
Recount
A full physical count. Import a CSV of counted quantities and post the adjustments.

Products

Define the catalog: products, brands, categories, units of measure, variants, and bulk import.

Open Products
Sidebar → Products. Use the toggle for table or grid view.
Add a product
Click “+ New Product”. Fill in information, pricing, inventory, and variants tabs.
Manage categories, brands, units
Use the sub-tabs inside the product modal or the settings page.
Bulk import (Excel)
Download the template, fill rows, upload. The system validates and reports row errors.
Bulk edit (spreadsheet mode)
Toggle bulk-edit on the table to edit prices inline for many products at once.
Activate / deactivate
Use the status toggle or select rows and bulk-activate / bulk-deactivate.
Bulk Excel import. Download the template from the Products page, fill in rows, then upload. Supported columns: name, SKU, barcode, category, brand, unit, cost price, selling price, tax rate, opening stock.

Customers

Build a customer CRM — loyalty points, store credit, purchase history, and outstanding balances.

Open Customers
Sidebar → Customers to see the CRM list.
Add a customer
Click “+ New Customer”. Enter name, phone, email, and loyalty tier.
Sell on credit
In POS, attach the customer and choose “Credit” as the payment method. Their balance updates immediately.
View history
Click any customer to see purchase history, loyalty points, and outstanding balance.
Redeem loyalty
At checkout, apply loyalty points as a discount if the customer has enough points.

Suppliers and Purchasing

Manage suppliers, raise purchase orders (POs), receive goods into stock, and track payables.

Add a supplier
Sidebar → Suppliers → “+ New Supplier”. Enter name, contact, and payment terms.
Raise a PO
Sidebar → Purchasing → “+ New PO”. Select supplier, branch, and line items. Submit for approval.
Approve a PO
A manager approves the PO. Stock is not affected yet.
Receive goods
Open the approved PO and click “Receive”. Enter quantities received. Stock-on-hand updates; a journal entry is posted to the inventory account.
Record supplier invoice
Match the PO to a supplier invoice; the payable is recorded in the general ledger.
Pay supplier
Issue a payment via cash or bank; the PO closes and the supplier balance reduces.

Reports

Generate sales summaries, profit and loss, VAT returns, and stock valuation for any period and branch.

Fig 5. Sales summary report
Open Reports
Sidebar → Reports and choose Sales Summary, Profit and Loss, VAT, or Stock Valuation.
Pick a period
Use the date pickers or the quick period chip: Today / This Week / This Month / Quarter / Year.
Pick branches
Choose All Branches or specific branches.
Run the report
Click “Generate”. KPIs and charts populate instantly.
Export
Click Export CSV (for data) or Export PDF (for a printable report).
Schedule
Accountants can schedule recurring reports to be emailed monthly.
Every report page has Export CSV and Export PDF buttons. CSV gives you raw data for spreadsheets; PDF gives you a printable layout for sharing.

Analytics

Interactive dashboards: ABC analysis, revenue trends, top products, staff performance, peak hours.

Top products by revenue (sample)

Visualize which products generate the most revenue. Export for further analysis.

Accounts and Finance

Chart of accounts, journal entries, ledgers, VAT, and financial statements.

Chart of accounts
Settings → Accounting → Chart of Accounts. Define asset, liability, equity, income, expense accounts.
Post a journal entry
Accounting → Journal → New. Enter date, debit and credit lines. The entry must balance before posting.
View ledgers
Ledgers show all entries for an account in a date range with running balance.
Generate statements
Reports → Profit and Loss or Balance Sheet. Exports to PDF for sharing.
VAT
Reports → VAT Return. Generates the output VAT and input VAT for the period and the net payable.

API and Exports

All list pages expose a REST API at /api and support CSV export. Here is how.

Authentication

The frontend uses JWT access and refresh tokens. The token is sent as Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. Access tokens expire every 15 minutes and are refreshed automatically on 401 responses. 

POST /api/auth/login/
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "email": "you@example.com",
  "password": "your-password"
}

Refreshing the token

POST /api/auth/refresh/
Authorization: Bearer <refresh_token>

Listing resources

GET /api/products/?search=bread&category=groceries&ordering=-created_at
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

# Response shape:
{
  "count": 128,
  "next": "https://…/api/products/?page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [ {…}, {…}, … ]
}

Audit trail / Logs

Most authenticated endpoints accept Accept: text/csv instead of JSON to return a CSV stream directly.
